question: Which of the following are used as soil binders?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pteridophytes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pteridophytes**

 
 
• Pteridophytes are a group of vascular plants that reproduce via spores.
 
• They lack seeds and flowers.
 
• Examples include ferns and horsetails.
 
• **Vascular tissue:** They possess xylem and phloem for efficient transport of water and nutrients.
 
• **Alternation of generations: **Their life cycle involves both a diploid sporophyte and a haploid gametophyte stage.
 
• **Spore dispersal: **They reproduce through spores, which are dispersed by wind or water.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fungi **

 
 
• Fungi are a diverse group of organisms that lack chlorophyll and cannot photosynthesize.
 
• They obtain nutrients by absorbing organic matter from their environment.
 
• Examples include mushrooms, yeasts, and molds.
 
• Heterotrophic nutrition: They rely on external sources of food.
 
• Cell wall: Their cell walls are composed of chitin.
 
• Reproduction: They reproduce through spores, either sexually or asexually.
 
 
 
• **Algae**
 
 
• Algae are a diverse group of photosynthetic organisms that lack true roots, stems, and leaves.
 
• They live in water or moist environments. Examples include seaweed, diatoms, and green algae. Key characteristics include:
 
 
 
• **Photosynthetic:**
 
 
• They produce their own food through photosynthesis.
 
• Aquatic habitat: Most algae live in water, although some can survive in moist terrestrial environments.
